stem: A hospital pharmacy does not hold a Drug Store license. A hospital employee asks it to fill an outpatient prescription for the employee's spouse. The spouse has lived at a separate address for six months and is not a hospital patient. What is the best conclusion under the Massachusetts institutional-dispensing rule?

choices.text: The pharmacy may dispense because legal marriage alone places the spouse within the employee-family category.
The pharmacy may dispense if the employee promises to deliver the medication personally.
The pharmacy may not rely on the employee-spouse exception because the spouse does not reside in the same household as the employee.
The pharmacy may dispense because household status matters only for an employee's child, not a spouse.
The pharmacy may dispense any outpatient prescription written by a hospital practitioner, regardless of the recipient.

explanation.core_reasoning: A hospital or clinic pharmacy that lacks a Drug Store license has a limited institutional-dispensing exception for specified recipients. An employee's spouse or child qualifies through that employee relationship only when the spouse or child resides in the same household. The marital relationship alone does not satisfy the added household condition.

choice_analysis.A: Incorrect. Marriage is not the only condition; the same-household requirement also applies.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. Who transports the medication does not alter the recipient eligibility rule.
choice_analysis.C: Correct. The spouse's separate residence prevents use of the employee-family exception on these facts.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. The household limitation applies to both an employee's spouse and child.
choice_analysis.E: Incorrect. Practitioner affiliation does not convert the limited exception into general retail dispensing authority.

related_facts: The restriction applies to institutional pharmacies operating without a Drug Store license.
Recipient status is evaluated independently from who wrote the prescription.
A family relationship and common household are distinct factual elements.
explanation.mpje_trap: Do not stop at the word spouse; the employee-family exception adds a same-household requirement.

stem: A pharmacist discovers that an improper warfarin dispensing caused a patient to be hospitalized, and the facts meet the serious-injury reporting criteria in 247 CMR 20.02(1). Which statements correctly distinguish the duties triggered by this same event? Select ALL that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacist’s initial QRE documentation remains subject to the 24-hour discovery-or-notification clock.
The seven-business-day Board reporting period is measured from the date the prescription was originally written.
The manager of record must report the qualifying improper dispensing within seven business days of discovery of the related serious injury or death.
Completing the QRE record eliminates the separate serious-event report because both rules concern the same dispensing error.
The event can trigger both CQI documentation and the separate serious-event reporting pathway because the rules have different purposes and clocks.

explanation.core_reasoning: A serious improper dispensing can activate two separate frameworks. The QRE record is initially documented within 24 hours after discovery or notification, while the manager-of-record report under 247 CMR 20.02(1) is due within seven business days of discovering the serious injury or death related to the improper dispensing.

choice_analysis.A: The QRE documentation duty retains its own 24-hour trigger even when the event is also reportable.
choice_analysis.B: The Board-report clock is not measured from prescription issuance; the relevant §20.02(1) trigger is discovery of the serious injury or death related to improper dispensing.
choice_analysis.C: This states the actor, event category, trigger, and seven-business-day reporting period for the improper-dispensing pathway.
choice_analysis.D: Internal CQI documentation does not substitute for the separate Board report once the reporting criteria are met.
choice_analysis.E: The same facts can satisfy both regulatory systems without merging their triggers or deadlines.

related_facts: 247 CMR 20.02(2) uses a different employee-knowledge trigger for a separate serious adverse drug event category involving pharmacy-manufactured, produced, or compounded products.
Warfarin errors can qualify for serious-event reporting when the regulation’s injury criteria are met.
explanation.mpje_trap: Do not blend the 24-hour QRE clock, the §20.02(1) discovery trigger, and the separate §20.02(2) employee-knowledge trigger.

stem: A pharmacist lawfully dispensed a three-day emergency oral Schedule II prescription after speaking directly with the prescriber. Eight days later, the pharmacy still has not received the required follow-up prescription despite documented requests to the prescriber. What federal step now becomes important for the pharmacist?

choices.text: Convert the emergency dispensing into a Schedule III refill so the existing record can remain open.
Delete the emergency prescription record because the prescriber failed to complete the follow-up.
Wait until 30 days after the oral authorization because the prescriber still has the full Schedule II validity period.
Reverse the original dispensing claim and treat the medication as an undocumented sample.
Notify DEA of the prescriber's failure to deliver the required emergency follow-up prescription.

explanation.core_reasoning: This question starts after the emergency dispensing has already occurred. Once the prescriber misses the required follow-up deadline, the pharmacist's issue is no longer whether the emergency was valid but what federal post-dispensing notification duty applies.

choice_analysis.A: A Schedule II emergency dispensing cannot be converted into a Schedule III refill.
choice_analysis.B: The dispensing record must be retained; deletion would not resolve the missed follow-up duty.
choice_analysis.C: The emergency follow-up rule uses its own seven-day deadline.
choice_analysis.D: Billing reversal does not change the legal fact that an emergency Schedule II dispensing occurred.
choice_analysis.E: After the seven-day follow-up failure, federal law places a DEA-notification duty on the pharmacist.

related_facts: The emergency oral Schedule II pathway has a seven-day follow-up requirement.
The pharmacist has a separate duty when the prescriber fails to deliver that follow-up.
explanation.mpje_trap: Memorizing 'seven days' is incomplete; know what the pharmacist must do when day seven passes without the follow-up.

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist administers a patient-specific dose of Abilify Maintena under the mental-illness administration pathway. Shortly afterward, the patient develops a severe reaction requiring emergency medical services and evaluation in an emergency department. Which follow-through actions are consistent with current Massachusetts guidance? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Immediately report the adverse event to the prescriber because emergency-department treatment is one of the specified serious outcomes
Record the adverse outcome or adverse event in the pharmacy's administration record
If the event is a dispensing error or a serious adverse drug event, fulfill the pharmacist's or intern's applicable Board reporting responsibility
Delay prescriber communication until the next routine reassessment because the patient has already been transferred to emergency care
Omit the event from the pharmacy record when emergency medical services create their own clinical documentation

explanation.core_reasoning: Massachusetts guidance treats adverse-event follow-through differently from routine post-administration communication. Emergency-department treatment is a specified serious outcome requiring immediate prescriber reporting, and adverse outcomes/events are part of the pharmacy administration record. Separate Board reporting duties continue to apply when the event is a dispensing error or serious adverse drug event.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. Additional treatment, testing, or monitoring in a hospital or emergency department is a listed serious outcome requiring immediate reporting to the prescriber.
choice_analysis.B: Correct. The administration record includes any adverse outcome or adverse event.
choice_analysis.C: Correct. The guidance preserves applicable Board reporting responsibility for a dispensing error or serious adverse drug event.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. A specified serious outcome is not handled by waiting for routine reassessment or ordinary communication timing.
choice_analysis.E: Incorrect. Outside emergency documentation does not replace the pharmacy's own required administration record.

related_facts: Adverse events that do not meet a listed serious-outcome trigger should still be appropriately communicated to the prescriber within 24 hours.
explanation.mpje_trap: Applying the guidance's strongly encouraged routine communication standard to a serious adverse event that has an immediate reporting trigger.

stem: A known Massachusetts prescriber telephones a new warfarin prescription to the pharmacist. Warfarin is a Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription drug. Which actions correctly apply to this oral prescription? Select all that apply.

The pharmacist should immediately reduce the oral prescription to writing with the information required by Massachusetts law.
The pharmacist must demand a replacement electronic prescription within two days because §20(c) applies identically to Schedule VI.
The Schedule VI exception from the later follow-up document does not eliminate the pharmacist's ordinary authenticity and validity responsibilities.
The pharmacist must convert the prescription to Schedule V before an oral transmission can be accepted.

explanation.core_reasoning: Massachusetts separates the immediate oral-prescription record from the later follow-up-document rule. Schedule VI is excepted from the latter, not from the pharmacist's contemporaneous documentation and validity duties.

choice_analysis.A: The Schedule VI exception concerns the later follow-up document; the pharmacist still immediately reduces the oral prescription to writing.
choice_analysis.B: Section 20(a) requires contemporaneous reduction of the oral controlled-substance prescription to writing.
choice_analysis.C: Section 20(c) expressly states that its later electronic/written follow-up requirements do not apply to Schedule VI.
choice_analysis.D: Schedule VI remains a prescription controlled substance under Massachusetts law; the follow-up exception is not a blanket validity waiver.
choice_analysis.E: An oral Schedule VI prescription does not become Schedule V; classification is not changed by transmission method.

related_facts: M.G.L. c. 94C §20(a) applies to oral controlled-substance prescriptions.
Section 20(c) expressly excludes Schedule VI from its later follow-up prescription requirement.

stem: A pharmacy filled a prescription, but the patient never picked it up and the medication never left the pharmacy's control. Staff want to return the tablets to inventory by pouring them back into the manufacturer's stock bottle. What is the appropriate Massachusetts approach?

The medication may be returned to stock under pharmacy policy in an appropriately identified return-to-stock container, without commingling it with manufacturer stock.
The medication may be poured into the manufacturer stock bottle because it never left the pharmacy or reached the patient.
The medication must be dispensed to another patient promptly or destroyed because prepared prescriptions cannot remain available for later reuse.
The medication may be returned to the manufacturer stock bottle after the first patient identifying information is removed from pharmacy records.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.13 distinguishes medication prepared but never dispensed from medication returned after leaving pharmacy control. Never-dispensed medication may be returned to stock under required controls, but the regulation prohibits returning it to the manufacturer's stock bottle and requires appropriate product-identifying container information and recall safeguards.

choice_analysis.A: The regulation permits a controlled return-to-stock pathway for medication never dispensed.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: return to stock is possible, but not by returning tablets to the manufacturer's stock bottle.

choice_analysis.D: There is no 24-hour dispense-or-destroy rule in this return-to-stock provision.
choice_analysis.E: Computer-profile changes do not authorize commingling with manufacturer stock.

explanation.mpje_trap: Never dispensed is the key fact, but it does not authorize commingling with the manufacturer's stock bottle.

stem: A Massachusetts sterile compounding pharmacy is replacing an ageing cleanroom air handling unit with an identical new one in the same position. Its director says a like-for-like swap changes nothing and needs no filing. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A like-for-like replacement falls outside the approval requirement.
Board approval is required before replacing any secondary engineering control.
Ordinary layout drawings suffice, since the configuration is unchanged.
The submission includes certified blueprints with ISO classification of each control.
Approval may be sought after the work if the pharmacy suspends compounding.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 6.15(2) requires a sterile compounding pharmacy to apply for Board approval PRIOR TO MOVING, ADDING, MODIFYING, REMOVING OR REPLACING ANY SECONDARY ENGINEERING CONTROL and bars it from doing so until approval is received. Under 6.15(4) the submission includes CERTIFIED blueprints depicting compounding areas and the location and ISO CLASSIFICATION of each primary and secondary engineering control, a containment strategy, an environmental monitoring plan, a re-certification plan and a continuity of care plan, each as applicable.

choice_analysis.A: Replacing is one of the five verbs the regulation names.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: prior approval is required.
choice_analysis.C: Certified blueprints with ISO classification are required.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: that is the first item on the list.
choice_analysis.E: The approval must precede the work.

related_facts: A re-certification plan and a continuity of care plan are included as applicable
explanation.mpje_trap: Candidates reason from whether the configuration changes rather than from whether a control is touched.

stem: A customer at a Massachusetts pharmacy counter asks to buy 5 grams of pseudoephedrine base today. He mentions that he bought 5 grams elsewhere eleven days ago. Which statements about the federal quantity limits are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: A regulated seller may sell him up to 7.5 grams in a single calendar day.
The pharmacy is the party federally restricted to 3.6 grams per purchaser per day.
Today's sale would exceed the 3.6 gram daily seller restriction.
Buying a further 5 grams within the 30-day window would put the purchaser over the 9 gram limit.
The 9 gram limit applies to sellers rather than to purchasers.

explanation.core_reasoning: The two limits bind different parties under different instruments. 21 CFR 1314.20(a) restricts a regulated seller from selling any purchaser more than 3.6 grams of pseudoephedrine base in a single calendar day, so a 5 gram sale is over the seller's daily ceiling. 21 U.S.C. 844(a) makes it unlawful for any person to purchase at retail more than 9 grams during a 30-day period, so a purchaser who already bought 5 grams eleven days ago would cross that prohibition. The 7.5 gram figure in 21 CFR 1314.20(b) is a 30-day limit and applies to mobile retail vendors.

choice_analysis.A: 7.5 grams is a 30-day figure for mobile retail vendors, not a daily allowance.
choice_analysis.B: The daily restriction does bind the seller, but this option omits that the sale here exceeds it.
choice_analysis.C: Correct: 5 grams in one day is above the 3.6 gram daily seller restriction.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: 5 plus 5 grams inside 30 days crosses the 9 gram retail purchase prohibition.
choice_analysis.E: The 9 gram limit is framed as a prohibition on the person purchasing at retail.

related_facts: Massachusetts requirements apply alongside the federal limits rather than instead of them
explanation.mpje_trap: Three real figures are in play and each belongs to a different party or period, so a candidate who remembers the numbers but not who they bind can pick any of them.

stem: A pharmacy manager audits a consultation space. Patients can enter it from the public side without passing through the dispensing area or stockroom. The opening has a waist-high divider, ordinary conversations can be heard in the waiting line, and a small sign reads "Counseling Room." Which changes are needed to satisfy the Massachusetts consultation-area requirements? Select all that apply.

choices.text: Display prominent signage designating the space as the "Patient Consultation Area."
Add features that provide visual privacy for consultations.
Add sound-control features sufficient to provide auditory privacy.
Relocate the space so patients must enter through the dispensing area before each consultation.
Replace privacy features with a staff escort whenever sensitive information will be discussed.

explanation.core_reasoning: The designated consultation area must have prominent identifying signage, provide both visual and auditory privacy, and remain accessible without requiring a patient to traverse the dispensing area or stockroom. The existing access route already satisfies the access component, but the generic sign, open sight lines, and audible conversations leave three separate defects.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. The regulation calls for prominent signage designating the space as the Patient Consultation Area.
choice_analysis.B: Correct. The waist-high divider does not provide the required visual privacy.
choice_analysis.C: Correct. Conversations audible from the waiting line show that auditory privacy is not provided.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. The current public-side route is compliant; requiring passage through the dispensing area would undermine the access requirement.
choice_analysis.E: Incorrect. An escort does not replace the physical requirement for visual and auditory privacy.

related_facts: Signage, privacy, and physical access are cumulative design requirements.
A consultation area can be within the licensed pharmacy while remaining accessible from the public side.
Auditory privacy requires evaluating what persons outside the space can hear.
explanation.mpje_trap: A compliant access path does not establish that the same space also satisfies signage and privacy requirements.

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy is fitting out a new prescription area. It proposes a dorm-style refrigerator with a small freezer compartment inside the refrigerator space for the few frozen products it stocks, with a continuous temperature logger fitted. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The pharmacy may not use an appliance with a freezer compartment inside the refrigerator space.
A freezer unit must be frost-free with an automatic defrost cycle unless the Board approves otherwise.
A continuous logger showing in-range temperatures makes the appliance acceptable.
The pharmacy's procedures must include a response protocol for any out-of-range temperature.
A combination refrigerator/freezer unit would not be permitted either.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 9.22(2) permits a combination refrigerator/freezer, a standalone refrigerator or a standalone freezer, requires freezer units to be frost-free with an automatic defrost cycle unless the Board otherwise approves, and states that a pharmacy may not use an appliance containing a freezer compartment within the refrigerator space, such as a dorm-style refrigerator. 247 CMR 9.22(1) requires policies including a protocol to respond to any out of range temperature and an assessment of the integrity of the medication.

choice_analysis.A: Correct: the dorm-style appliance is named in the prohibition.
choice_analysis.B: Correct: frost-free with automatic defrost, unless otherwise approved by the Board.
choice_analysis.C: Monitoring is a separate duty; it does not make a prohibited appliance permissible.
choice_analysis.D: Correct: the response protocol is part of the required policies.
choice_analysis.E: A combination refrigerator/freezer is one of the three permitted configurations.

related_facts: Temperatures are measured and maintained in accordance with Board guidance
explanation.mpje_trap: Good monitoring makes the appliance feel defensible. The regulation prohibits the appliance itself, so the quality of the logging never comes into it.

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy receives a prescription for generic buprenorphine sublingual tablets for opioid use disorder with a 90-day quantity. Which quantity rule should the pharmacist apply?

choices.text: A 30-day ceiling applies to every Schedule III opioid.
Every Schedule III prescription permits a 90-day fill.
The initial-opiate seven-day limit controls OUD treatment.
The OUD pathway may permit one fill of up to 90 days.
Five refills may be combined into one 90-day fill.

explanation.core_reasoning: Massachusetts permits a single fill of up to a 90-day supply for a Schedule II or III drug used to treat opioid use disorder, unless another law prohibits it. Generic buprenorphine sublingual tablets fit that indication-specific pathway.

choice_analysis.A: The OUD pathway is an express exception to the general 30-day rule.
choice_analysis.B: The 90-day permission depends on the drug and indication, not Schedule III status alone.
choice_analysis.C: The initial-opiate limit does not govern a drug prescribed for OUD treatment on these facts.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. The prescription may qualify for a single fill of up to 90 days.
choice_analysis.E: Refill authorization does not determine the quantity allowed in one fill.

related_facts: Current generic buprenorphine sublingual tablets are used to treat opioid dependence and are Schedule III.
Subutex was the legacy brand for buprenorphine sublingual tablets; the Subutex brand product is discontinued, while generic presentations remain available.
M.G.L. c.94C, §23(d) permits up to a 90-day single fill for Schedule II or III drugs used to treat OUD.
explanation.mpje_trap: Use the current generic presentation; do not present discontinued Subutex as a current brand product.

stem: A supplier receives a paper DEA Form 222 twenty days after execution. The form is otherwise timely, but the purchaser altered a Schedule II quantity after signing by writing over the original number. The purchaser asks the supplier to initial the change and ship the order. What is the best response?

choices.text: Fill the order because the form arrived within 60 days and timeliness cures execution defects.
Fill only the unaltered line items and correct the altered line after shipment.
Convert the altered paper form into a CSOS order by scanning it and adding an electronic signature.
Do not fill the defective form; the purchaser must issue a proper replacement order despite the original form still being within 60 days.
Wait until day 61 and then fill the form because expiration removes the need to address the alteration.

explanation.core_reasoning: A valid Form 222 must satisfy both execution/content rules and the time window. Here the form is timely but defective, so the supplier cannot use the 60-day rule to overlook the alteration.

choice_analysis.A: The 60-day validity period does not cure an altered or defective form.
choice_analysis.B: A supplier may not correct and fill a defective executed form in that manner.
choice_analysis.C: A paper Form 222 is not converted into a valid CSOS order by scanning it.
choice_analysis.D: Defect/execution validity is an independent gate from the 60-day time window.
choice_analysis.E: Expiration would create an additional reason not to fill the order, not cure the alteration.

related_facts: Form validity involves more than age.
A defective Form 222 cannot be corrected by the supplier and then filled as though properly executed.
explanation.mpje_trap: When two gates apply, passing the timing gate does not cure a separate execution defect.

stem: On Friday morning, a pharmacy discovers a significant unexplained loss of controlled substances. The investigation cannot be completed that day. Which federal response is correct?

Give oral notice within 24 hours and take no further action.
File Form 106 within one business day instead of separate notice.
Send written DEA notice within one business day and Form 106 within 45 calendar days.
Notify only the Massachusetts Board because the loss occurred in Massachusetts.

explanation.core_reasoning: The registrant must give the responsible DEA Field Division written notice within one business day of discovery. The separate complete and accurate electronic DEA Form 106 is due within 45 calendar days after discovery, allowing the investigation to inform the documentation without delaying initial notice.

choice_analysis.B: Oral notice alone does not satisfy the written notice and Form 106 duties.

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacist resolved a criminal matter in another state by admitting to sufficient facts, and the case was continued without a finding and later dismissed. She tells the Board she has no conviction to report. How should that resolution be characterised for Board purposes?

Not a conviction, because no sentence was ever imposed upon her.
Not a conviction, because the matter arose outside of the Commonwealth.
A conviction only if the Board separately finds that she committed the crime.
A conviction, because an admission to sufficient facts and a continuance without a finding are included.

explanation.core_reasoning: 247 CMR 10.02 defines conviction to include any admission to or finding of sufficient facts to warrant a finding of guilt, regardless of adjudication, a continuance without a finding, and any plea of guilty or nolo contendere, of or to a crime in any jurisdiction, accepted by the court, whether or not a sentence has been imposed. Each of the features she relies on is expressly inside the definition.

choice_analysis.A: Regardless of adjudication is part of the definition, so a later dismissal does not remove it.
choice_analysis.B: The definition applies whether or not a sentence has been imposed.
choice_analysis.C: The definition reaches a crime in any jurisdiction.
choice_analysis.D: No separate Board finding is needed; the definition applies on its own terms.
choice_analysis.E: Correct: both features named are inside the regulatory definition.

related_facts: A conviction of a person licensed by the Board is conclusive evidence of the commission of that crime in a disciplinary proceeding based upon it.
explanation.mpje_trap: The regulatory definition is broader than the ordinary meaning and expressly covers a continuance without a finding.

stem: During prospective drug utilization review, the pharmacy system flags a clinically significant conflict. Which statements correctly describe the Massachusetts requirements? Select all that apply.

The pharmacist must document the measures taken in response to the DUR finding, not only a prescriber call.
A certified pharmacy technician may resolve the clinical conflict independently when an approved protocol supplies the decision steps.
Every DUR finding requires prescriber consultation before dispensing, regardless of the pharmacist's clinical assessment.
Documentation is optional when the pharmacist addresses the issue directly with the patient rather than the prescriber.

explanation.core_reasoning: After identifying a DUR concern, the pharmacist selects appropriate responsive measures. Consultation with the prescriber, patient, or patient agent is an available response rather than a universal requirement for every alert. Whatever measures the pharmacist takes must be documented. A certified pharmacy technician's expanded technical scope does not include performing DUR or resolving clinical conflicts.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. Massachusetts leaves the responsive measure to the pharmacist's professional judgment and identifies consultation as a possible measure.
choice_analysis.B: Correct. The documentation duty attaches to the measures taken, not merely to telephone contact with a prescriber.
choice_analysis.C: Incorrect. Clinical DUR and conflict resolution remain outside certified technician scope even when a protocol exists.
choice_analysis.D: Incorrect. Prescriber consultation is not mandated for every DUR finding; the pharmacist chooses an appropriate response.
choice_analysis.E: Incorrect. The duty to document is not waived because the pharmacist's chosen measure involved the patient instead of the prescriber.

A DUR response can differ with the nature and seriousness of the identified problem.
The response decision and the documentation duty are separate questions.
explanation.mpje_trap: Do not confuse a permitted consultation option with a mandatory prescriber call, and do not let technician certification expand into clinical conflict resolution.

stem: A referred patient at a Massachusetts retail pharmacy has run out of a medication her supervising physician prescribed, and the physician is unreachable. The collaborating pharmacist has never dispensed this patient a different medication for the same condition. What may the pharmacist do under the retail collaborative power?

Extend the current therapy the supervising physician prescribed by 30 days.
Extend the current therapy indefinitely until the physician can be reached.
Substitute a therapeutically similar agent and notify the physician afterwards.
Nothing, because the retail setting confers no continuation power at all.

explanation.core_reasoning: The retail limb of the statute confers an extension by 30 days of CURRENT drug therapy PRESCRIBED BY THE SUPERVISING PHYSICIAN. It is a continuation power over the physician's own therapy, not a power to start something new, and it is bounded at 30 days.

choice_analysis.C: The power is bounded at 30 days.

The February 2026 modifications became fully effective on August 8, 2026 and must be treated as implemented today

The Board may grant an extension beyond the limit.
The limit does not yet apply if the individual has not reached 18 years of age.
The limit is suspended whenever the employing pharmacy is short staffed.
An individual who exceeded the limit before turning 18 must apply for a technician licence within 30 days of the 18th birthday.

Employer staffing pressure is not among the exceptions.

stem: A Massachusetts pharmacy operating under a Commissioner vaccine order is revising its written protocols. It already covers training and adverse-event response. Which proposed decisions correctly identify additional protocol subjects that 105 CMR 700.003(F)(2)(b) expressly requires? Select all that apply.

Add a regulation-mandated written-consent protocol before every administered dose.
Retain procedures for return of vaccine even if unused doses are uncommon.
Add a regulation-mandated rule to report every dose to the immunization registry within 24 hours.
Retain recordkeeping procedures for vaccine administration.

explanation.core_reasoning: 105 CMR 700.003(F)(2)(b) requires written protocols addressing proper storage, handling and return of vaccine, recordkeeping regarding administration, response to adverse events, and safe and appropriate administration. The stated paragraph does not add the specific written-consent or 24-hour registry reporting mandates used as distractors.

choice_analysis.E: Correct: recordkeeping regarding administration is expressly named.

related_facts: Proper training, supervision and adverse-event response also remain part of the pathway.

stem: During a controlled-substance review, a supplier plans to ship the unfilled balance of a DEA Form 222 order 64 days after execution. What is the problem?

choices.text: Ship the balance because 60 business days have not elapsed.
Extend the form by documenting the supplier's back order.
Use the original form indefinitely for any unfilled balance.
The ordinary 60-day Form 222 validity and partial-shipment window has expired.
Change the execution date after the purchaser agrees.

explanation.core_reasoning: 'The ordinary 60-day Form 222 validity and partial-shipment window has expired.' is the governing result. By contrast, 'Ship the balance because 60 business days have not elapsed.' would require that 21 CFR 1305.13 measured business rather than calendar days. The decisive cue appears in 'During a controlled-substance review, a supplier plans to ship the unfilled balance of a DEA Form 222 order 64 days after execution. What is the problem?'.

choice_analysis.A: 'Ship the balance because 60 business days have not elapsed.' would apply only if 21 CFR 1305.13 measured business rather than calendar days; 'During a controlled-substance review, a supplier plans to ship the unfilled balance of a DEA Form 222 order 64 days after execution. What is the problem?' states otherwise.
choice_analysis.B: 'Extend the form by documenting the supplier's back order.' would apply only if a back order created an extension beyond the 60-day period; 'During a controlled-substance review, a supplier plans to ship the unfilled balance of a DEA Form 222 order 64 days after execution. What is the problem?' states otherwise.

Which description of the order’s ordinary fulfillment period is correct? Select ONE answer.

The ordinary 60-day fulfillment period has ended; do not ship the remainder under this expired order.
Use the patient-prescription 30-day rule instead of the stock-order rule.
A new 60-day period starts on first shipment day 20.

stem:

Under the federal requested-partial rule, which date starts the 30-day completion limit? Select ONE answer.

choices.text: October 9, the first partial dispensing date.
October 2, the prescription issue date.
The date the patient next telephones the pharmacy.
The date the pharmacy's wholesaler delivers replacement stock.

stem: A pharmacy prepared and labeled a prescription, but the patient never picked it up and the medication was never dispensed. The pharmacy is evaluating whether to return the medication to stock under 247 CMR 9.13. Which statements are correct? Select all that apply.

choices.text: The never-dispensed medication may be returned to stock if the rule's container, labeling, expiration, and recall safeguards are satisfied.
The medication may be poured back into the manufacturer's stock bottle because the patient never possessed it.
It may remain in the original patient container, or be placed in an appropriate container bearing the required product identifiers and the expiration date assigned when the prescription was filled.
The pharmacy must maintain procedures that permit identification and removal of the returned-to-stock medication if it is later recalled.
Once prepared for a patient, the medication is treated as previously dispensed even when it never left the pharmacy, so return to stock is categorically barred.

explanation.core_reasoning: Massachusetts permits return to stock for medication that was prepared for dispensing but was never actually dispensed. The medication may not be placed back into the manufacturer's stock bottle. It may remain in the original patient container or be placed in an appropriate container that preserves the required product identifiers and the expiration date assigned when filled, and the pharmacy must retain recall-identification safeguards.

choice_analysis.A: Correct. Never-dispensed status opens the return-to-stock pathway, subject to all stated safeguards.
choice_analysis.B: Incorrect. The regulation specifically prohibits returning the medication to the manufacturer's stock bottle.
choice_analysis.C: Correct. The rule permits the original patient container or an appropriate container with required identity and filled-expiration information.
choice_analysis.D: Correct. Recall procedures must allow the pharmacy to identify and remove affected returned-to-stock medication.
choice_analysis.E: Incorrect. Preparation is not the same as dispensing; the rule expressly covers prepared medication that was never dispensed.

related_facts: Required identifiers include the drug name, strength or concentration, and manufacturer, supplier, or national drug code information.
The expiration date used for return to stock is the date assigned when the prescription was filled.
This pathway is distinct from attempted reuse of medication previously delivered to a patient.
explanation.mpje_trap: Do not confuse prepared with dispensed, and do not assume never leaving the pharmacy permits commingling with the manufacturer's stock bottle.
